newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE May white sugar jumps off lows before expiry.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE May white sugar jumps off lows before expiry.

text.p: Nearby white sugar positions see-sawed in Tuesday afternoon trading as players scrambled to bale out of the spot May contract before expiry at close of business, traders said.
With under two hours to go in the last session before May goes off the board, most holders of spot positions have already squared their books to avoid being involved in physical deliveries.
One talking point in the market was the amount of sugar expected to be delivered against May, especially the likely extent of the outstanding long positions.
Traders have estimated amounts of between two and 10 cargoes, although the most recent calculations based on uncovered positions suggested around five, they said.
"Obviously people's eyes are glued to what's happening on May," said one trader.

Light trade and commission house buying dragged May off its session low of $302.60 but the nearby May/August spread remained at a discount through most of the day while August/October and other spreads were at premiums.
Against actuals trades on May between commission houses also boosted the overall volume.
At 1620 GMT May was down $2.10 at $304.40, with the second-month August contract more expensive at $308.60, down 30 cents on the day. Volume was a solid 3,126 lots.
Some commission house selling of the August/July white premium was noted at around $65, slightly wider than Tuesday's close.
Only the front three months were traded in Paris where total volume reached 1,115 lots.
May was down $2.50 at $306.50 and August up 20 cents at $308.50.
